items.title: Start here: a quiz engine that grew create, update and delete
items.body:
This repo is a Java 17 command-line quiz engine. It started as "load questions from a file and run a quiz" and was extended with create, update and delete, which is where the interesting engineering lives.

The classes, smallest first:

- **Question** - one immutable question: id, prompt, 2 to 26 choices, the correct letter, an optional explanation.
- **QuestionAttempt** and **QuizResult** - one chosen answer, and the result of a quiz session.
- **QuizEngine** - asks questions and reads answers; it never touches files.
- **QuestionLoader** - the original parser for the old pipe-separated file.
- **QuestionBank** - owns the current questions and every write to disk.
- **App** - the menu and the forms.

Read astraupskill/ in this order: README, 01-CODEBASE-MAP (its table says which lines own which job), 02-CONCEPTS, 03-WORKED-CHANGE, 04-TESTING-AND-DEBUGGING, 07-TRACE-LAB. Try 05-PRACTICE before opening 06.

Compile src/quiz and test/quiz with javac and run quiz.QuestionBankTest to see all 28 cases pass.

items.title: How the quiz loop treats input that is not a valid letter
items.body:
**Key: two retry prompts, then a is read as A and graded as one attempt.**

readValidAnswer trims and upper-cases each line with Locale.ROOT, then accepts it only if it is exactly one character between A and the last label. Z is out of range and ab is two characters, so each prints "Please enter a letter from A to D." and the loop asks again. a becomes A, which is valid and is graded. Only that answer becomes a QuestionAttempt; the regression test checks one attempt and one correct answer.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Z graded as wrong**: invalid input is retried, never graded.
- **Lowercase refused**: the input is upper-cased before the check.
- **ab graded on its first letter**: isValidAnswer requires length 1.

excerpts.quote: String input = scanner.nextLine().trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
invalid quiz input retries without an extra attempt

items.title: Why an update cannot rename a question
items.body:
**Key: IllegalArgumentException, and both the file and the list keep Q1 as it was.**

update first compares the id argument with the replacement's id and throws "An update cannot change the question id." when they differ. It then checks that the id exists. Both checks run before a candidate list is built or commit is called, so nothing is written and nothing is published. The regression test "update missing or changed identity leaves original" compares the file text afterwards.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Renamed in place**: identity is what the record is; the code refuses to change it through update.
- **Q2 created as new**: update never creates; a missing id is also an error.
- **IOException from commit**: commit is never reached, so no lock or byte comparison happens.

excerpts.quote: if (!id.equals(replacement.getId())) throw new IllegalArgumentException("An update cannot change the question id.");
update missing or changed identity leaves original

items.title: Core idea: two file formats and what a quiz result counts
items.body:
**Files.** The bank can be read from two formats. Open data/questions.txt to see the original one: one question per line, fields split by pipes, choices split by semicolons. Then read serialize and parse in QuestionBank to see the newer versioned format: a header line, one row per question, and a footer line. Write down how each format would cope with a pipe or a tab inside a prompt, and which method decides which parser to use when a file is opened.

**Quiz results.** QuizEngine and QuizResult keep several counts apart: questions planned for the session, questions answered, correct, incorrect. Read QuizResult and note which count each getter uses as its denominator. Then read readValidAnswer in QuizEngine and list what it does with input that is not a usable answer, and what it returns when input runs out.

The trace lab asks you to fill a table of these counts yourself before comparing with its expected rows. Do that first.

items.title: Why a stale session keeps failing until it restarts
items.body:
**Key: B's delete is rejected with the same stale message, because B's remembered bytes never refresh.**

Each QuestionBank remembers the bytes it loaded in a field called original. commit compares the current file with original under the lock, and only assigns a new original (and new questions) after a successful move. A's create changed the file. B's create failed the comparison and returned before that assignment, so B still remembers the old bytes, and its delete fails the same comparison. There is no reload command, so B must exit and restart.

Why the others are wrong:
- **The failed create refreshed B's copy**: the refresh line runs only after the move succeeds.
- **Q2 is lost**: the comparison exists to stop exactly that overwrite.
- **B waits on the lock**: tryLock does not wait, and A released the lock when its save finished; the stale bytes are the problem.

excerpts.quote: original = serialized; questions = List.copyOf(candidate);
because `original` is refreshed only by a successful commit

items.title: When a legacy bank becomes a versioned file
items.body:
**Key: the file is unchanged after the load and the quiz, and becomes a QUIZ-BANK versioned file after the create.**

The constructor reads the bytes and, for a file that does not start with QUIZ-BANK, uses QuestionLoader. It writes nothing; the first regression test checks the bytes are identical after loading a legacy bank. Running a quiz never writes either. The create calls commit, which serializes the whole candidate with serialize, and that method always emits the versioned header, rows and footer.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Rewritten at load**: loading is read-only by design, so a legacy file you only read stays as it was.
- **Still pipe-separated after create**: there is no code that writes the legacy format.
- **Written at exit**: there is no save-on-exit; each accepted command is written by commit before its success message.

excerpts.quote: legacy bank loads without rewriting bytes
StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder(HEADER).append

items.title: Why an empty legacy file fails but an empty versioned bank loads
items.body:
**Key: the comments-only legacy file stops startup, while the empty versioned bank loads.**

QuestionLoader skips comment lines and then throws "Question file does not contain any questions." when nothing is left. QuestionBank.parse has no such rule: a header followed by END and 0 is a valid bank with zero rows. That is how deleting the final question works (a regression test reloads the empty bank). The course flags the mismatch as an inconsistent contract and practice exercise 5 asks you to fix it.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Both load as empty**: the legacy loader refuses an empty result.
- **Both stop startup**: the versioned parser accepts END 0, and the "deleting final question" test depends on it.
- **The versioned one fails its footer check**: END followed by a tab and 0 matches the expected footer for zero rows.

excerpts.quote: if (questions.isEmpty()) { throw new QuestionFileException("Question file does not contain any questions."); }
deleting final question leaves reloadable empty bank

items.title: Why a correct answer of d fails with three choices
items.body:
**Key: IllegalArgumentException, because the correct answer does not match any choice.**

The constructor upper-cases the correct-answer label with Locale.ROOT, so "d" becomes D, index 3. validateCorrectAnswer converts the label to an index and throws "Correct answer does not match any choice." when the index is not below the number of choices. With three choices only A, B and C exist. A lowercase c would have been accepted and stored as C.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Stored as lowercase d**: the label is always upper-cased in the constructor.
- **Answer D that nothing matches**: the constructor refuses to build such a question; that is the invariant.
- **Labels must be uppercase**: lowercase input is normalized, not rejected.

excerpts.quote: this.correctAnswer = requireText(correctAnswer, "Correct answer").toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
throw new IllegalArgumentException("Correct answer does not match any choice.");

items.title: Why an unknown version header is refused instead of guessed
items.body:
**Key: the constructor rejects it as an unknown format, without trying the legacy parser.**

The constructor sends any text starting with QUIZ-BANK to parse. parse requires the first line to equal the exact header for version 1 (QUIZ-BANK, a tab, 1). A file saying 99 fails that check and gets "Unknown or incomplete question bank format." The regression test "unknown bank format never falls back to legacy" pins this.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Falls back to the legacy parser**: the prefix check routes the file to parse, and parse has no fallback.
- **Loaded with the version 1 parser**: parse compares the whole first line, not just the prefix.
- **An empty bank from the footer**: the header check fails before the footer is read.

excerpts.quote: throw new QuestionFileException("Unknown or incomplete question bank format.");
unknown bank format never falls back to legacy

items.title: What the learner sees for a missing question file
items.body:
**Key: "The quiz could not be started:" followed by just the bare file path.**

The QuestionBank constructor's first real step is Files.readAllBytes. For a missing file that throws NoSuchFileException, whose message is only the path. App.run catches IOException and prints "The quiz could not be started: " plus that message, then returns. Running the app on nope.txt prints exactly that.

Why the others are wrong:
- **"Question file was not found."**: that text lives in QuestionLoader, which is only reached after the bytes were read, so it is dead code on this path.
- **Welcome and an empty menu**: a missing file is not treated as an empty bank; run returns before printing Welcome.
- **A stack trace**: run catches the exception, so nothing escapes main.

excerpts.quote: this.original = Files.readAllBytes(this.file);
out.println("The quiz could not be started: " + error.getMessage()); return;

items.title: How the versioned format stores pipes, semicolons and tabs
items.body:
**Key: each text field is Base64-encoded, so delimiters inside the text leave rows intact.**

serialize writes id, prompt, explanation and every choice through encode, which is Base64 of the UTF-8 bytes. Base64 output uses only letters, digits, +, / and =, so it never contains a tab or a newline, the two characters the format uses to split fields and rows. parse splits on tabs and decodes each field with unpack. A regression test round-trips pipes, semicolons, tabs, backslashes and newlines.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Backslash escaping**: 02-CONCEPTS says Base64 is used precisely to avoid inventing escaping.
- **Pipes between fields, choices on their own lines**: fields are tab-separated and a question is one row.
- **Double-quoted fields**: there is no quoting; that is a CSV technique this code does not use.

excerpts.quote: Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))
Base64 allows pipes, semicolons, tabs and newlines without inventing ambiguous escaping.

items.title: Which message a non-numeric choice count produces
items.body:
**Key: Invalid input: For input string: "abc"**

edit calls Integer.parseInt on the text before it checks the 2 to 26 range. parseInt throws NumberFormatException, which is a subclass of IllegalArgumentException. The menu loop catches IllegalArgumentException and prints "Invalid input: " plus the exception message, which for parseInt is the JDK text. Running the app with abc piped in prints exactly that line.

Why the others are wrong:
- **"Choose 2 through 26 choices."**: that message comes from the range check, which runs only after a successful parse.
- **"Not saved: ..."**: that prefix is for IOException from the bank; nothing reached the bank.
- **The menu-number message**: that is printed for an unknown menu choice, not for a form field.

excerpts.quote: int count = Integer.parseInt(rawCount);
catch (IllegalArgumentException | NullPointerException error) { out.println("Invalid input: " + error.getMessage()); }

items.title: How an interrupted quiz is summarized
items.body:
**Key: 1 of 2 answered, 1 unanswered, and a score of 100.00% on the answered one.**

When input runs out, readValidAnswer returns null, askQuestion returns null and runQuiz stops. It builds QuizResult with the attempts so far and the planned count. The result reports answered and unanswered separately, and getFinalScorePercent divides correct answers by answered attempts, so one correct out of one answered is 100%. The app prints "Quiz interrupted; partial result only." and labels the score as covering answered questions.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Missing one counted wrong, 50%**: an unanswered question is not an attempt, so it is neither correct nor incorrect.
- **Quiz finished, both graded**: only one answer was given; isComplete is false.
- **No summary**: the engine checks hasNextLine first, so Scanner never throws here.

excerpts.quote: return (getCorrectCount() * 100.0) / getTotalQuestions();
EOF midway does not count unanswered as incorrect

items.title: What happens when input ends at the delete confirmation
items.body:
**Key: it prints "Deletion cancelled." and the question stays in the bank.**

read returns null when the scanner has no next line. delete compares the confirmation with "yes".equalsIgnoreCase(confirm). Calling equalsIgnoreCase with null returns false, so the cancel branch prints "Deletion cancelled." and returns without calling the bank. Piping "7", then "Q1", then ending input shows exactly that.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Nothing more is printed**: that is what happens when input ends at the earlier id prompt, which returns silently. At the confirmation prompt the cancel message is printed.
- **Missing answer as consent**: only an answer equal to yes, ignoring case, confirms.
- **"Input ended. The incomplete edit was not applied."**: that message belongs to the create/update form, not to delete.

excerpts.quote: if (!"yes".equalsIgnoreCase(confirm)) { out.println("Deletion cancelled."); return; }
return scanner.hasNextLine() ? scanner.nextLine().trim() : null;

items.title: Core idea: three commands, one place that writes
items.body:
Create, update and delete in QuestionBank each do the same three things: check identity, build a **candidate** list (the next state, not yet visible), and pass it to one private method, commit. None of them writes to disk itself. That gives the project one write boundary to reason about instead of three.

Read commit slowly and number its steps. For each step write two notes: what the learner sees if this step fails, and which of the bank's fields (questions, original) have changed by that point. Then do the same for a second QuestionBank object that was loaded from the same file earlier.

Two words from the glossary help here. A **candidate** is the next list, validated before anything is written. **Publication** is the moment the bank makes that list its visible state. Finding exactly where publication happens, relative to the file replacement, is the key to most of the persistence behaviour in this pack.

excerpts.quote: Each one validates identity, builds a *candidate* list, and then hands that candidate to the same `commit`; none of them writes to disk itself.

items.title: Why a missing footer rejects the whole bank
items.body:
**Key: startup refuses the whole bank, reporting an invalid footer.**

parse treats every line between the header and the last line as a question row, and requires the last line to be exactly END, a tab and the number of rows read. With the END line cut off, the last remaining line is a question row, so the comparison fails and parse throws "Missing or invalid bank footer." wrapped as "Invalid question bank: ...". App reports that the quiz could not be started.

Why the others are wrong:
- **Complete rows load**: the footer exists to detect truncation; nothing is loaded from a bank that fails it.
- **The last row dropped**: there is no partial recovery; the whole file is refused.
- **Legacy parser takes over**: the first line still starts with QUIZ-BANK, so the versioned parser is chosen.

excerpts.quote: throw new IllegalArgumentException("Missing or invalid bank footer.");
truncated footer rejects whole bank
